Shortest paths, connected components, clustering, and assortativity

topology.Rd

Native C++23 graph topology and descriptive network algorithms: unweighted (BFS), non-negative weighted (Dijkstra), and negative-weight (Bellman–Ford) shortest distances and path reconstruction, exact and pseudo-diameter, connected and strongly connected components (with attractor detection), Hopcroft–Tarjan biconnected components (articulation points and bridges), topological sorting and DAG testing, local and global clustering coefficients (with jackknife standard error), and scalar/categorical assortativity.

Usage

shortest_distance(graph, source = NULL, target = NULL, weights = NULL,
                  max_dist = Inf)
shortest_path(graph, source, target, weights = NULL)
pseudo_diameter(graph, source = 1L, weights = NULL)
graph_diameter(graph, weights = NULL)
label_components(graph)
label_biconnected_components(graph)
topological_sort(graph)
is_dag(graph)
local_clustering(graph)
global_clustering(graph)
assortativity(graph, values = "total", categorical = FALSE, weights = NULL)

Arguments

graph

An rgraphtool_graph object.

source

Optional 1-based source vertex ID(s). When NULL in shortest_distance(), computes all-pairs distances in parallel.

target

Optional 1-based target vertex ID(s).

weights

Optional edge property name or numeric vector of edge lengths / weights.

max_dist

Maximum distance cutoff for shortest_distance().

values

For assortativity(), "total", "in", or "out" for degree assortativity, a vertex property name, or a length-\(N\) vector.

categorical

Logical; if TRUE, computes discrete Newman assortativity rather than scalar Pearson correlation.

Value

shortest_distance() returns a numeric vector (for a single source) or matrix. shortest_path() returns list(vertices, edges, distance). pseudo_diameter() returns list(diameter, endpoints) and graph_diameter() returns a scalar. label_components() returns list(membership, sizes, num_components, attractors). label_biconnected_components() returns list(edge_component, num_components, articulation_points, bridges). topological_sort() returns an integer vertex ordering and is_dag() returns a logical scalar. local_clustering() returns a length-\(N\) vector, global_clustering() returns a named length-2 vector c(clustering, std_err), and assortativity() returns a numeric correlation coefficient.

Examples

g <- graph_create(6L, directed = FALSE)
graph_add_edges(g, rbind(c(1, 2), c(2, 3), c(3, 1), c(3, 4), c(4, 5), c(5, 6), c(6, 4)))
shortest_path(g, 1L, 6L)
#> $vertices
#> [1] 1 3 4 6
#> 
#> $edges
#> [1] 3 4 7
#> 
#> $distance
#> [1] 3
#> 
label_biconnected_components(g)
#> $edge_component
#> [1] 3 3 3 2 1 1 1
#> 
#> $num_components
#> [1] 3
#> 
#> $articulation_points
#> [1] 3 4
#> 
#> $bridges
#> [1] 4
#> 
global_clustering(g)
#> clustering    std_err 
#>  0.6000000  0.1844551 
assortativity(g, "total")
#> [1] -0.1666667
